title: Preserve where hydraulic force acts before using a pressure-biased threshold
statement: In the symmetric source bridge a=b=c=K0>0,bottom=K0*d,d>0, let Delta>0,k>=0, delta0=Delta*(1-d)/[2*(1+d)] and R=(3+d)/[2*K0*(1+d)]. Equal-and-opposite closing forces Fb on the two midpoints give delta=(delta0-R*Fb)/(1+k*R) and a positive neutral d=(K0*Delta-3*Fb)/(K0*Delta+Fb), when that value is physically admissible. If only the test midpoint receives closing force Fb and the reference receives none, delta=[delta0-Fb/(K0*(1+d))]/(1+k*R), with neutral d=1-2*Fb/(K0*Delta). These are different force interfaces.

requires: Positive symmetric Hookean bridge in quasistatic equilibrium; Delta>0, k>=0, known force directions/attachments and one common force/length unit.
Paired formula: equal opposite forces on both midpoint nodes. Single-test formula: zero reference force, closing force on test only. Restrict each zero to positive physically admissible d.

assumptions: Source one-midpoint wording and full-R formula are not interchangeable; no arbitrary hydraulic geometry is certified.
A pressure source can supply power while changing the sensing interface. Balancing and residual force must be established in the actual device.

contract.units: K0,k are force/length; R length/force; Fb,Fr,Ft forces; Delta,delta lengths; d dimensionless.
contract.obstruction: Acquire actual pressure-force placement and balance before importing an unbiased mechanical threshold into powered flow control.

body: Let A=2*K0 and B=K0*(1+d). Before probe coupling, adding closing reference force Fr and closing test force Ft changes the free midpoint gap by -Fr/A-Ft/B. Coupling the spring gives delta=[delta0-Fr/A-Ft/B]/(1+k*R), R=1/A+1/B. Set Fr=Ft=Fb to obtain the full differential-compliance formula and solve K0*Delta*(1-d)=Fb*(3+d). Set Fr=0,Ft=Fb for the separate one-test-node formula. The supplied bias_checks substitutes the closed-form zero into biased_readout; it does not solve a newly forced matrix. This resolves a source wording conflict: biased_bridge_zero says force to one midpoint, while biased_readout uses R*Fb. The rational threshold is accepted only for a conjugate force pair, not that literal one-node description. For Fb>=0 a positive paired threshold requires Fb<K0*Delta/3; a positive single-test threshold requires Fb<K0*Delta/2. Other signed forces/attachments require the actual equilibrium and admissible state. At fixed nonzero bias, changing drive changes Fb/(K0*Delta), so the unbiased sign law cannot be transferred unchanged to the powered pilot. Pressure-balanced diaphragms are a proposed way to reduce bias; their balance, switching work and biological compatibility are not acquired.
